flawed_step: Lines 0014–0016 incorrectly claim that f cannot belong to T1; the argument overlooks the possibility f=e.
counterexample: Let V={x,y} and T1=T2={{x,y}}. Choose e={x,y}. Then T1−{e} has components VA={x} and VB={y}. The unique T2-path from x to y consists only of e, so the constructed crossing edge is f=e. Thus f belongs to T1, contrary to line 0014.
assessment_summary: The proof contains a false concrete claim: its constructed edge f need not be distinct from e or absent from T1. In the explicit two-vertex example, f=e. Although exchanging that common edge still yields trees, lines 0014–0016 are incorrect as written.
